{{Short description|Number that is its own Gödel number}}
In [[number theory]] and [[mathematical logic]], a '''Meertens number''' in a given [[number base]] <math>b</math> is a [[natural number]] that is its own [[Gödel numbering|Gödel number]]. It was named after [[Lambert Meertens]] by [[Richard S. Bird]] as a present during the celebration of his 25 years at the [[Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica|CWI]], [[Amsterdam]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=[[Richard S. Bird]] |year=1998 |title=Meertens number |journal=[[Journal of Functional Programming]] |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=83–88 |doi= 	 10.1017/S0956796897002931|s2cid=2939112 }}</ref>

== Definition ==
Let <math>n</math> be a natural number. We define the '''Meertens function''' for base <math>b > 1</math> <math>F_{b} : \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}</math> to be the following:
:<math>F_{b}(n) = \prod_{i=0}^{k - 1} p_{k - i - 1}^{d_i}. </math>
where <math>k = \lfloor \log_{b}{n} \rfloor + 1</math> is the number of digits in the number in base <math>b</math>, <math>p_i</math> is the <math>i</math>-th [[prime number]] (starting at 0), and 
:<math>d_i = \frac{n \bmod{b^{i+1}} - n \bmod b^i}{b^i}</math>
is the value of each digit of the number. A natural number <math>n</math> is a '''Meertens number''' if it is a [[Fixed point (mathematics)|fixed point]] for <math>F_{b}</math>, which occurs if <math>F_{b}(n) = n</math>. This corresponds to a [[Gödel encoding]].

For example, the number 3020 in base <math>b = 4</math> is a Meertens number, because 
:<math>3020 = 2^{3}3^{0}5^{2}7^{0}</math>.

A natural number <math>n</math> is a '''sociable Meertens number''' if it is a [[periodic point]] for <math>F_{b}</math>, where <math>F_{b}^k(n) = n</math> for a positive integer <math>k</math>, and forms a [[Periodic sequence|cycle]] of period <math>k</math>. A Meertens number is a sociable Meertens number with <math>k = 1</math>, and a [[Amicable numbers|amicable]] '''Meertens number''' is a sociable Meertens number with <math>k = 2</math>.

The number of iterations <math>i</math> needed for <math>F_{b}^{i}(n)</math> to reach a fixed point is the Meertens function's [[persistence of a number|persistence]] of <math>n</math>, and undefined if it never reaches a fixed point.
